# Toy bricks — Style Prompt

> A stop-motion film of studded plastic bricks on a real desk, shot like macro toy photography: a low lens at brick height, glossy plastic with clean softbox highlights, the real room (a teapot, a cup, a stack of books) melted into soft focus behind. A small brick-built robot acts in big held poses on twos while the camera holds still or glides on ones; a tall build wobbles, tips and breaks into bricks that bounce and settle, and the parts fly back on arcs to become something better. Hard cuts between a handful of set-ups; one dark subtitle pill, low and centred, carries the words.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

A toy world on a **real surface** under a **macro lens**, animated **in stop-motion**. The charm is the tension between the tiny world and the big room: the desk becomes a landscape, a teapot a mountain, and every action is something a child could do with their hands (stack, knock over, sort, rebuild). Failure is harmless: what falls apart becomes spare parts.

One-glance traits: glossy bricks with a bright top edge and a soft rectangular highlight; profile studs on every top edge; dark seams where bricks meet; a green studded baseplate in steep perspective, sharp at the focus row and soft before and behind it; a dark grey launch plate edged with yellow and black tiles; real objects out of focus; a white brick robot with a round helmet, a wrap-around navy visor and two white dot eyes; motion that steps (12 drawings a second) while the camera moves smoothly.

Characters are **built from bricks**: 1×1 columns for legs on grey foot plates, a grey 2×2 hip plate, two 2×2 bricks for the torso with three coloured buttons, arms of three round 1×1 bricks, a grey collar plate, a round 2×2 double-height helmet with four studs on top, a visor wrapped two radians around it and a thin antenna with a glowing red tip. Never a trademarked toy name, logo or minifigure silhouette, and no lettering on studs.

Not a low-poly island (no faceted shading, no floating diorama), not clay or felt (bricks never bend, squash or morph), not a clean product render (this world is knocked over and rebuilt), not a flat cartoon (light, depth of field and gloss carry the realism).

## 2. Materials & rendering

The source renders in 3D with clearcoat plastic, area-light softboxes, ambient occlusion and physical depth of field. Mosio rebuilds the same frames in 2D, painted once and then only moved:

- **Units are studs.** 1 = one stud pitch; brick height 1.2, plate 0.4, studs 0.48 wide and 0.18 tall with a lighter lip, bevel 0.07. Every size, height and distance below is in studs, turned into pixels by the set-up's pixels-per-stud.
- **One canvas per camera set-up**, painted at load from a seeded PRNG at half resolution (the look is soft) and turned into an image: studio wall gradient (from `--latar`), grey desk with faint grain (from `--latar-2`), the props, the baseplate, out-of-focus foreground pieces.
- **Brick**: rounded front face with a vertical gradient (top 24% lighter, bottom 20% darker), the far side 17% darker, a soft softbox reflection (white 34% fading down, on the upper-left third), a 2.5% bright top line, a 3.5% dark AO line at the bottom, studs as shaded cylinders. Seen from above: a lighter top face and studs as ellipses (height 0.38 of width).
- **Baseplate** in true perspective: camera height `h` studs above the plate, focal length 1500 px (about the source's 32–46° lenses), rows `z` near to far, each stud a dark side, a light top and a specular dot, one path per row. Depth of field = rows grouped into bands composited with blurs from 0 (focus row) to 9 px (nearest), like the source's circle of confusion ∝ |1/focus − 1/z|.
- **The robot** (rig of the source, 8.9 studs tall with the antenna): parts painted once at 150 px per stud. Arms pivot at (±1.5, 5.5); a pose is `[forward, side]` in radians, shown as a rotation by the side angle and a vertical scale of cos(forward), so an arm reaching at the lens shortens and arms raised overhead (forward −2.9) flip up. The helmet is a shaded cylinder; nod tilts it (top face and studs appear, visor drops), look turns it (the visor and eyes slide around the cylinder: visor edges at 1.17·sin(look ± 1), eyes at look ± 0.31). Three-quarter view: right side faces 20–36% darker. Sitting lowers the body 2.25 studs and folds the legs to 12%.
- **Effects are bricks**: nothing is a particle system or a soft gradient.
- **Grade**: a vignette darkening the corners by 36% (smoothstep from 25% to 85% of the radius), no grain.

## 3. Colour logic

- `--latar` is the **studio wall** (12% darker at the top, 12% lighter at the horizon) and `--latar-2` the **desk**. A white brand gives a white studio, a dark brand a night desk.
- `--utama` is the **hero brick red** of the source palette: the stripes of the tall tower (red at bricks 1, 4, 8 and 11 of 12, from the bottom) and its cone, the brick the robot carries, half the rebuilt tower, the big name brick, one chest button. `--teks-di-utama` is the print on it.
- `--aksen` is the **signal yellow**: the hazard tiles along the launch plate, the brick icon in every subtitle pill, the small sign (with `--teks-di-aksen`), one chest button.
- Fixed in every brand, because they are the toy box and the room (the source palette): plastic white `#f4f4f1`, baseplate green `#53a63b`, launch plate grey `#4f514b`, tile black `#1b2a34`, visor `#0f2036`, toy blue `#0055bf`, orange `#fe8a18`, tan `#e4cd9e`, light grey `#a0a5a9`, dark grey `#6c6e68`, azure `#36aebf`, dark green `#237841`, the reverse angle's dark backdrop `#2f2509` (mixed 6% toward `--latar`), ceramic `#d9c6ae`, cloth book spines `#7b2d26`, `#274b6d`, `#3d5c3a` with pages `#efe6d2`, antenna glow `#ff3b30`. The subtitle pill is `#12141a` at 62% with white text.
- Each built object has one dominant colour and at most two trims; the saturated colours belong to the toys, the room stays natural.

## 4. Type

- `--font-isi` carries the subtitles, exactly the source's pill: Fredoka 700 (the source's 600) at 46 px, one line, in a pill 84 px tall with radius 42, 30 px padding left and 40 px right, top at y 930, centred. A 58×26 px brick icon in `--aksen` (two 18×10 studs, an 18% darker bottom band) leads every line, 22 px from the text.
- `--font-judul` carries titles printed on bricks: Fredoka 700 at 112 px on a 1160×212 px name brick, 58 px on a 580×106 px small brick stacked on it.
- When the brand has no fonts: rounded and friendly (Fredoka 500/700, Poppins 800 for a printed brick). Wide brand fonts: keep the brick and shorten the words; never shrink the subtitle under 40 px.

## 5. Motion quality

The example plays the source's timings × 1.25 (its 12 s excerpt becomes 15 s); physics stays real time.

- **Two clocks**: the robot, bricks and titles step at **12 fps** (`steps(n)` with n = seconds × 12, or one `tl.set` per drawing); camera moves and shakes run smooth.
- **Wobble** before a fall: rocking about the base edge by 0.025·sin(2π·2.1·w)·(w/1.67) + 0.01·w radians, w = seconds since the wobble began.
- **Tip, then break**: the tower tips as one body from 0.07 to 0.38 rad with θ'' = G/(1.6·Hc)·sin θ (0.41 s), then every brick is free: velocity = ω × r plus a kick of (r − 0.3)·6 sideways, (r − 0.5)·9 in depth, r·3 up (studs/s), gravity G = 420 studs/s² (toy gravity, slower than true), restitution 0.28, friction 0.72, spin ×0.6 per contact, a 6% pull toward lying flat per contact, rest under 2.5 studs/s after 0.6 s, bricks pushed apart under 2.6 studs so they never stack. Precomputed at 240 Hz, sampled at 24, shown at 12. A brick that ends turned shows its 4-stud side.
- **Fly-in**: a piece flies 0.45 s on an arc (`eio` ease, lift 5 + 0.3 × row studs), one every 0.19 s, arrives 0.35 stud high and drops 0.35 → 0.18 → 0 over two drawings: the click.
- **Acting**: big poses held at least 0.5 s, changes over 2–7 drawings. Nervous: arms out 0.45–1.05 rad, head up 0.45. Alarm: arms up 2.6 rad and a 1.1-stud hop backwards over 0.5 s. Sad: arms drop to 0.1, head down 0.35–0.5, sit over 0.56 s. Pick up: arm forward 1.2 rad, head turns 0.25. Cheer: a 0.9-stud hop with arms raised from −0.6 to −2.9 over 0.3 s.
- **Camera shake** on the fall: up over 0.2 s, held 0.3 s, gone 2.3 s later; a fresh random offset per 24 fps frame, up to ±22 px. A lighter 3 px shake while the table is being shaken.
- **Titles** pop on 12 fps steps with scale 0.6 + 0.5·sin(0.75πu) over 0.25 s (0.6, 0.95, 1.1, then 1). **Subtitles** appear and vanish on a cut, no transition.
- **Ending**: everything lands by 13.0 s and holds 2 s.

## 6. Camera grammar

| Move | Expresses | Can serve |
|---|---|---|
| Low wide at brick height, looking up, static (lens 46°, camera 1.6 studs above the desk) | The build is tall, the maker small | an opening; a goal; "look what we made" |
| Low frontal on the build, static, 25 studs away, then a handheld shake | Something is about to happen to it | the test; a risk; a failure |
| Reverse-angle close-up on a dark backdrop, straight dolly in about 15% over the whole shot (linear) | Feeling, a decision | the lesson; disappointment; an idea |
| Close static medium at torso height, head cut by the frame | Hands at work | steps; picking up; assembling |
| Wide over the desk with props and spare parts | The scale reveal | the payoff; the call to action; a summing-up |
| Top-down plan over the baseplate | Order, a map | a plan; sorting parts; a timetable |
| Tracking alongside a moving build, destination ahead | Momentum | a launch; a journey; a race |

Cut on actions (a click, an impact, a sit-down); no dissolves. Keep foreground clutter soft at the frame edges and check headroom in every shot.

## 7. Native moves

- **Snap-together building.** Pieces fly in on arcs, one every 0.19 s, and click home; the character places the last one. *Fits content like:* a kids' class building a bridge; a bakery stacking a layer cake brick by brick; a creator's channel growing video by video; a house built for a new neighbour in a story.
- **Break without harm.** A wobble, a tip, a heap of spare parts that bounce and settle under a handheld shake. *Fits content like:* a plan that failed before the right one; "what happens without a foundation" in a science lesson; an old phone case that cracks before the new one; the setback in a short story.
- **Toy on a real desk.** Real objects become landscape, soft behind the action. *Fits content like:* a keyboard as a city grid for a coding course; a coffee cup as a tower for a café opening; a stack of books as cliffs for a reading club; a houseplant jungle for a gardening channel.
- **Held poses on twos.** The robot sits down, bows its head, looks up, reaches for a brick: one pose per beat, held. *Fits content like:* a student's "aha" for a tutoring service; a reaction for a creator's skit; a shop mascot showing the product; a quiet sad moment in a story.
- **Rebuild into something else.** The same pieces fly back as a better object: the thin tower becomes a wide one. *Fits content like:* a before/after renovation; a career change; a menu reworked; a team reshuffled.
- **The scale reveal with a printed brick.** Back to the wide: the hero stands on its build with arms up while the name brick pops into the set. *Fits content like:* a class's weekend schedule; a toy shop's opening day; a creator's channel name; a year in review.

## 8. Pitfalls

- **Performance**: never redraw bricks or studs per frame. Paint each set-up once (half resolution is enough) and turn it into an image; move only images with transforms, promote the moving ones (`will-change: transform`) so a step does not repaint the whole set, and update the collapse only when its 12 fps drawing changes and its shot is on screen. Blur is painted into the canvas, never a CSS filter on moving elements, and only over the band that holds the content.
- **Load time**: thousands of studs are fine as one path per row and colour; a canvas filter per brick is not (every filtered draw blurs a full-size layer).
- **Orange whites**: the plastic white is a fixed cool white; never mix it toward a warm `--latar`.
- **Pasted-on bricks**: without the AO line and the bright top line, stacked bricks look like stickers; without depth-of-field bands, the baseplate looks like wallpaper.
- **A stepped camera** or smooth characters both break the medium: characters on twos, camera on ones.
- **Explosions**: a collapse falls and bounces low; the free-body velocities come from the tip, not from a blast.
- **Text**: titles live on bricks, subtitles in the pill, both above the action (the pill's top at y 930: keep the build's base above it). Never words straight on the wall.
- **Shake edges**: a shaken set is scaled 3% so its edges never show.
- **Trademarks**: no toy brand name, logo, minifigure silhouette or stud lettering.

## Measured from the reference

12 s reference at 24 fps, 5 shots: 0.92 / 3.58 / 4.5 / 1.33 / 1.67 s (median 1.67 s, 20 cuts a minute, first cut at 0.92 s): a static low wide of the wobbling tower, the frontal collapse (impact about 0.45 s after the fall starts, heap settled within 1 s, held 2 s), the long reverse-angle close-up where the robot sits and looks up under a slow dolly, a static medium of the robot picking up a brick and standing, and a wide over the parts pile. Brightness light, light, dark (the reverse angle), mid, mid. Palette: wall `#c6d0da`/`#adbfd4`, desk `#a5a4a7`, plate green `#53a735`, red brick `#cf2a1e`, launch plate `#383a32`, white in the shade `#d4d3e0`, visor `#031630`, backdrop `#2d2104`. The example scales the cuts to 1.15 / 5.6 / 11.0 / 12.6 s and holds its ending 2.4 s.

# Toy bricks: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 1.2, medium 2.4, long 4.5.

## hook

- en: low macro wide at brick height: the build stands tall in a soft real room, the brick character watching it, camera still
- id: lebar dan rendah setinggi balok: bangunan berdiri di ruangan nyata yang kabur, tokoh balok menatapnya, kamera diam

## problem

- en: the table shakes, the build rocks, tips and breaks into bricks that bounce and settle; handheld shake on impact
- id: meja diguncang, bangunan bergoyang, tumbang, pecah jadi keping yang memantul lalu diam; kamera ikut terguncang

## fact

- en: reverse-angle close-up on a dark backdrop, slow straight dolly in; the character sits, then lifts its head, poses held
- id: close-up dari arah sebaliknya berlatar gelap, kamera maju pelan; tokoh duduk lalu mengangkat kepala, pose ditahan

## step

- en: pieces fly in on arcs, one every 0.19 s, and click home with a small drop; the character places the last one
- id: keping terbang melengkung tiap 0,19 detik lalu klik terpasang; tokoh memasang keping terakhir

## compare

- en: two builds side by side on one baseplate: the thin one shaken apart, the wide one still standing
- id: dua bangunan berdampingan di satu baseplate: yang kurus runtuh diguncang, yang lebar tetap berdiri

## number

- en: the figure printed on a brick that pops in on 12 fps steps, a stack of bricks beside it as the counter
- id: angka dicetak di balok yang muncul bertangga 12 fps, tumpukan balok di sampingnya sebagai penghitung

## proof

- en: a finished build held in a low close-up, the character beside it in a proud pose, real props soft behind
- id: bangunan jadi dalam close-up rendah, tokoh di sampingnya berpose bangga, benda sungguhan kabur di belakang

## offer

- en: the product or class name printed on a big brick that pops into the set, the detail in the subtitle pill
- id: nama produk atau kelas dicetak di balok besar yang muncul di set, rinciannya di pil subtitle

## cta

- en: wide with the real props: the hero on its build, arms up, a printed name brick pops in, contact in the pill; held 2 s
- id: lebar dengan benda sungguhan: tokoh di atas bangunannya, lengan ke atas, balok nama muncul, kontak di pil; diam 2 detik

## payoff

- en: back to the whole desk: the rebuilt thing stands among spare parts, the character cheers; held 2 s
- id: kembali ke seluruh meja: bangunan baru berdiri di antara keping cadangan, tokoh bersorak; diam 2 detik
